q1_what_did_you_play: Rummage first for 1 energy, spending the 3-Spark bank to draw 3 cards. That leaves 3 energy and a hand that now contains the disclosed 1-energy 7-damage Attacks. Then Rapid Fire, which no longer shows 0 because the Sparks are gone, at its printed 2 energy into Seapunk (the only enemy, so all four 4-damage hits land on it) for 16. That leaves 1 energy, which I spend on one of the drawn 1-energy 7-damage Attacks for a total of 23 damage. I only list cards printed on this page in chosen_line; the third play is a drawn card whose title the page does not print, so I name it here instead of inventing a title. Seapunk ends around 23/46 and I take the full 11, going to 31/62.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes, two. The obvious one is Rapid Fire at its shown cost of 0 (consuming the Sparks) plus Duck and Cover for 1: 16 damage, 5 Block, only 6 damage taken. But that spends 1 of 4 energy and empties the hand, leaving 3 energy on the table, so I rejected it as pure waste. The near-miss was Rummage, Rapid Fire, Duck and Cover, which costs exactly 4 and gives 16 damage plus 5 Block. I rejected that because the point of Rummage is to convert the Sparks into cards I actually cast this turn; ending on Duck and Cover means two of the three drawn cards go unplayed, so I paid a card and a Spark bank for 5 Block I already had access to without Rummage.
q3_what_it_gave_up: All of the Block. Duck and Cover stays unplayed, so I eat the whole 11 instead of 6 — 5 extra HP off a pool that is already down 20. It also spent the Spark bank on Rummage rather than on the free Rapid Fire, meaning Rapid Fire cost me 2 real energy; the Sparks bought cards instead of a discount. And it burns through draw pile now rather than banking Duck and Cover's mitigation for a turn where I need it more.
q4_different_intent: Yes. Against 11 into 42 HP I can afford to race, because 5 HP is cheap and Seapunk's 46 needs three turns of pressure. If the telegraph were a big hit — say 20 or more — or if I were low enough that 11 threatened a two-turn death, I would take the Rummage / Rapid Fire / Duck and Cover version, or drop Rummage entirely and use the free Rapid Fire so I could hold energy for Block. Conversely, if Seapunk were blocking or buffing with no incoming damage at all, I would play the same cards but feel no tension about it — the 23-damage line becomes strictly correct rather than a trade.
